paper_title: Copper catalysis for highly selective aerobic oxidation of alcohols to aldehydes/ketones†

questions.question: In this paper, what does the abbreviation 'TEMPO' refer to (full chemical name as given in the text)?
What copper catalyst (formula and hydrate state) is identified and used as the optimal catalyst throughout the study?
In Table 1, which solvent was used in the reaction of 1-phenyl-2-heptyn-1-ol (1a) that gave 99% yield of 2a with 0% recovery of 1a (Table 1, entry 9)?
Which copper salt gave the higher yield of 2a in Table 2 — CuBr2 or Cu(NO3)2·3H2O — and what were the reported yields for each?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Cu(NO3)2·3H2O gave the higher yield: 96% (for 2a) vs CuBr2 which gave 12% (Table 2).

questions.question: Under the optimized Cu(NO3)2·3H2O/TEMPO/MeCN conditions reported in Table 3, what yield was obtained for the aerobic oxidation of terminal propargylic alcohol 1b to ketone 2b (report both NMR and isolated yields if provided)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 94% (NMR yield), with a 91% isolated yield (Table 3, entry 6).
